captions.search.compareLess: {key} is smaller than {node}, so the search goes left.
captions.search.compareGreater: {key} is larger than {node}, so the search goes right.
captions.search.found: {key} equals {node}, so the key is found.
captions.search.notFound: The {side} branch of {node} is empty, so {key} is not in the tree.
captions.insert.root: The tree is empty, so {key} becomes the root.
captions.insert.place: {key} goes into the empty {side} branch of {parent}.
captions.update: Node {node} now has a balance factor of {hr} − {hl} = {bf}.
captions.imbalance.insert: Node {node} has a balance factor of {bf}, so it is the first unbalanced node, n. This is Case {case} ({code}).
captions.imbalance.delete: Node {node} has a balance factor of {bf}, so it is unbalanced.
captions.rotate: Rotate {child} around {about}. This is a {dir} rotation about {about}.
captions.delete.remove: {key} is a leaf, so it is removed.
captions.done: Every node now has a balance factor of −1, 0 or +1.
captions.inorderCheck: The in-order sequence before the rotation is {before}. After the rotation it is {after}, so the BST order is unchanged.
captions.format: Numbers use a true minus sign (−). A negative height inside a subtraction is put in brackets, as in 3 − (−1).

search-loop: if element in node p equals el
return element in node p  // el was found
else if el < element in node p
return null  // el was not found
search-recursive: return null  // end of tree reached
else if element in root equals el
return element in root  // el was found
else if el < element in root

glossary.root: The root is the top node of a tree. It has no parent.
glossary.leaf: A leaf is a node with no children.
glossary.height: The height of a node is the number of edges on the longest path from that node down to a leaf. A leaf has height 0, and an empty branch has height −1.
glossary.balance factor: The balance factor (bf) of a node is the height of its right branch minus the height of its left branch.
glossary.AVL tree: An AVL tree is a binary search tree in which every node has a balance factor of −1, 0 or +1.
glossary.n: Node n is the first unbalanced node found on the way back up after an insertion.
glossary.rotation: A rotation is a local change that moves a child up around its parent without changing the in-order sequence.
glossary.single rotation: A single rotation is one left or right rotation. It fixes the outside cases, Cases 1 and 4.
glossary.double rotation: A double rotation is two rotations, first about a child of n and then about n. It fixes the inside cases, Cases 2 and 3.
glossary.in-order traversal: An in-order traversal visits the left subtree, then the node, then the right subtree. In a BST, it lists the keys in sorted order.
glossary.outside case: In an outside case, the new key went into the left subtree of n's left child (Case 1) or into the right subtree of n's right child (Case 4).
glossary.inside case: In an inside case, the new key went into the right subtree of n's left child (Case 2) or into the left subtree of n's right child (Case 3).
glossary.O(log n): O(log n) describes a cost that grows like the number of times n can be halved. For 1,000,000 keys, log₂ n ≈ 20.

questionTypes.mcq: The student chooses one option. Each wrong option is linked to a misconception and has its own explanation.
questionTypes.case-id: The student chooses one of the four cases. The options and the correct case come from the engine.
questionTypes.enter-values: The student enters heights or balance factors for the target nodes.
questionTypes.click-node: The student clicks a node. The target is the first unbalanced node, every node that breaks the AVL rule, or the parent of a new key.
questionTypes.trace: The student clicks the search path and then chooses Found or Not found.
questionTypes.perform-rotation: The student sees the tree right after the BST step and performs the rotation or rotations.
questionTypes.build-tree: The student carries out the operation, including any rebalancing, and builds the final tree.

wrongAnswerPatterns.goes-wrong-direction: A step in the trace goes left for a larger key or right for a smaller key.
wrongAnswerPatterns.visits-extra-nodes: The trace includes a node that is not on the search path.
wrongAnswerPatterns.rotated-at-root: The student rotates about the root when n is lower down.
wrongAnswerPatterns.rotated-wrong-direction: The student rotates the opposite way, left instead of right or right instead of left.
wrongAnswerPatterns.double-wrong-order: For an inside case, the student rotates about n first, or about the wrong child.
wrongAnswerPatterns.rotated-again-above-n: After fixing n, the student also rotates an ancestor of n.
